name: Michael Moritz

summary.text: Michael Moritz is a Welsh-born former Time journalist who was a Sequoia Capital partner from 1986 until 2023. He sat on the board of X.com/PayPal from August 1999 and on Google's from 1999 to 2007. His Crankstart Foundation reported $4.4 billion in assets for 2024. He has given £75 million to Oxford, financed San Francisco political groups (TogetherSF, about $17 million pledged) and founded the San Francisco Standard. He is a listed investor in California Forever, which spent over $800 million on Solano County farmland. Nationally he gave more than $15 million to Democrats in 2024, after earlier gifts to Republicans.

facts.claim: Moritz began as a journalist at Time magazine and joined Sequoia Capital in 1986. He gave up his management role there over a decade before leaving the firm in 2023, and later became a senior adviser to Sequoia's wealth-management arm.

sources.title: Great Immigrants: Michael Moritz

facts.claim: PayPal's 2001 registration statement lists Moritz as a director since August 1999 and a Sequoia partner since 1986. He was a managing member of SC IX Management, LLC, general partner of the Sequoia funds that held 9.9% of PayPal before the IPO; he disclaimed beneficial ownership except for his financial interest.

sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Form S-1/A

facts.claim: Speaking on Sequoia's podcast, Moritz said the firm did not know about Confinity, X.com's future merger partner, when it first invested in X.com.
facts.quote: We weren't aware of the presence of Confinity when we made the first investment in X.com.

sources.title: Crucible Moments, episode 1: PayPal ft. Max Levchin: A Merger of Enemies That Reshaped Silicon Valley

facts.claim: In September 2000, while Musk was on his honeymoon, PayPal managers went to Sequoia's headquarters to ask the board to remove Musk as CEO, and the board backed them in a meeting with Moritz. Peter Thiel became CEO.

facts.claim: Discussing eBay's 2002 offer of $1.5 billion, Moritz said Peter Thiel favored the sale and he did not.
facts.quote: Peter was very inclined to make the sale. I did not want to do that.

facts.claim: In July 2012 Moritz pledged £75 million for Oxford undergraduates from families earning under £16,000 a year, released in £25 million tranches as Oxford raised matching funds.

sources.title: Record donation to support poorest Oxford undergraduates

facts.claim: IRS data for the Crankstart Foundation (San Jose) list Moritz as CEO in 2024 and president/CFO in 2019–2023. The foundation reported total assets of $4.39 billion and about $206 million in charitable disbursements for 2024, up from $1.87 billion in assets in 2019.

sources.title: Crankstart Foundation

facts.claim: Moritz is TogetherSF's board chair and its main funder since it was founded in 2020. A July 2023 internal presentation said he and Crankstart had given $6 million and pledged $11 million more (total $17 million). Mission Local reported that he founded the San Francisco Standard in 2021 with $10 million, and he co-founded the political arm, TogetherSF Action, in 2022.

sources.title: TogetherSF wants to remake City Hall. Internal doc shows that's just the beginning.
Billionaire venture capitalist Michael Moritz looms big in coming election

facts.claim: In 2024 Moritz spent nearly $3.2 million backing San Francisco's Proposition D, a TogetherSF Action measure to expand the mayor's power and cut the number of city commissions. He also gave $600,000 to a committee run by mayoral candidate Mark Farrell to support it. Total pro-Prop D spending passed $9.5 million, and voters rejected it about 55% to 45%.

facts.claim: OpenSecrets data cited by CNBC show earlier Republican giving by Moritz: to Arnold Schwarzenegger, to Mitt Romney (2007) and to John Kasich's 2010 and 2014 Ohio campaigns. In 2024 he gave $4.8 million to American Bridge 21st Century, an anti-Trump group, and also gave to the Lincoln Project.

sources.title: Trump's tech backers are 'making a big mistake,' Sequoia's Mike Moritz says

facts.claim: By July 2024 Moritz had given about $7.8 million to pro-Biden and anti-Trump causes in the 2024 cycle. In an email to the New York Times he urged Biden to withdraw and said he would stop giving to Democratic fundraising appeals until then.

sources.title: Billionaire Democratic donor tells Biden to step aside: 'Vanity or virtue'

facts.claim: In an August 5, 2024 Financial Times op-ed, Moritz wrote that tech figures backing Trump, a group CNBC said included Marc Andreessen, Ben Horowitz, Elon Musk, David Sacks and his former partner Doug Leone, were "making a big mistake."
facts.quote: prepared to turn a blind eye to Trump

sources.title: Trump's tech backers are 'making a big mistake,' Sequoia's Mike Moritz says

facts.claim: Moritz gave $2.5 million in September 2025 to support California's Prop. 50, which replaced the state's independent congressional maps for three election cycles. The San Francisco Standard reported his 2024 contributions to Democratic candidates at more than $15 million.

sources.title: They led Sequoia Capital for decades. Now they're on opposite sides of Prop. 50.

facts.claim: Flannery Associates, a California Forever subsidiary, began buying Solano County farmland in 2018 and had spent more than $800 million on over 78 square miles near Travis Air Force Base by September 2023. Its Delaware registration kept investors anonymous until The New York Times named them in August 2023. Reps. Garamendi and Thompson had sought for years to identify the buyers.

facts.claim: California Forever lists Moritz among its investors, with Marc Andreessen, Patrick and John Collison, Chris Dixon, John Doerr, Nat Friedman, Daniel Gross, Reid Hoffman, Laurene Powell Jobs and Andreessen Horowitz. It calls them passive investors and says about 97% of its capital comes from US investors.

facts.claim: In May 2023 Flannery Associates sued several Solano County landowners in federal court, accusing them of conspiring to fix land prices.

facts.claim: On July 22, 2024, California Forever withdrew its Solano County ballot measure for a new city from the November 2024 ballot and said it would seek county approval in 2026 instead.

sources.title: California Forever abandons ballot measure in face of growing opposition, looks to 2026

facts.claim: In August 2026, a state bill backed by Assemblymember Lori Wilson and Sen. Christopher Cabaldon would designate 1,350 acres of the project's land as a maritime industrial zone using an 18-year-old environmental report. Solano County supervisors voted 3–2 to oppose it. The Standard, which named Moritz as a backer and its own chairman, reported this.

openQuestions: No reliable source was found on Moritz's personal stake or share of California Forever's roughly $1 billion in capital. A Puck report that Moritz was pitched in October 2017 and committed to help raise close to $1 billion could not be opened.
Moritz's role in creating Sequoia Capital China in 2005 (reported by The Information and Wikipedia as with Doug Leone) could not be confirmed from an opened source.

Bloomberg's November 2023 report that Moritz committed about $300 million to reshaping San Francisco could not be opened. Mission Local's figure of $4.4 million in SF campaign giving since 2003 and Inside Philanthropy's 'over $300 million' were not reconciled.
Mission Local reported $500,000 from Moritz to Farrell's Prop D committee and the SF Examiner reported $600,000; the city ethics filings were not checked.

FEC itemized records for Moritz were not retrieved (API rate limit). Totals ($7.8 million by July 2024; more than $15 million for 2024) come from news reports with different cutoffs. A $1 million Lincoln Project figure appears only in an advocacy-group source.
Moritz's 2003 letter to UC Treasurer David Russ dropping UC from Sequoia's Fund XI over public-records requests is reported by PlanSponsor, which could not be opened.
Whether the Crankstart Foundation itself holds interests in Sequoia funds was not checked in its Form 990-PF schedules.
